meaning: The cheatsheet prescribes how a parameter scan is run and read: a multiplicative grid over Ca_v, skipping failed points, and an amplitude statistic defined as per-cycle peak-to-trough with the median across cycles, measured only on the last 20 s. These are modelling choices about what "the" pulse amplitude means, not just coding tips.

could_move.what: Any m5 amplitude comparison against a recording, since the median-across-cycles peak-to-trough definition sets the number being matched
Reported best-fit Ca_v, because the multiplicative decade grid fixes which candidate points exist at all
Model-vs-data comparison deck, where model and data amplitude must use the same statistic
Model-vs-model decks, if the 20 s window truncates differently between models
Silently skipped grid points narrowing the curve that argmin then searches

expectation: Unknown. The reach trace found no code references to this cheatsheet, so I cannot tell from the context whether the fitting code follows these rules, nor how far fitted Ca_v would move if the window or statistic changed.

check.why: Shows whether the 20 s window, the median statistic and the Ca_v grid described here actually appear in the fitting code and target definitions, or whether the cheatsheet has drifted from them. Cheap text search, no solve.
